'''''Lithophyllum incrustans''''', also known by its common names '''coraline crust''' and '''paint weed''',<ref>{{cite book |author1=David Chapman |title=Exploring the Cornish Coast |date=2008 |publisher=Alison Hodge |location=[[Penzance]] |isbn=9780906720561 |page=31}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Os nomes galegos das algas |url=https://achave.gal/wp-content/uploads/achave_osnomesgalegosdas_algas_2020_4.pdf |website=A Chave |access-date=15 March 2023 |page=27 |language=gl |date=2020}}</ref> is a small pinkish species of [[seaweed]].<ref>{{cite WoRMS |author=Guiry, M.D. & Guiry, G.M. |year=2021 |title=Lithophyllum incrustans Philippi, 1837 |id=145152 |accessdate=}}</ref>

==Description==
This is a small encrusting,<ref>Fritch, F.E. 1965. ''The Structure and Reproduction of the Algae Volume 2.'' Cambridge University Press p 508</ref> calcareous alga, growing epiphytically as a flat lobed plant up to 10 cm in diameter and up to several mm forming thick adherent crusts. It can become knobbly with overlapping lobes and a smooth surface. In colour it is pinkish but may become bleached.<ref name =Irvine>Irvine, L.M. and Chamberlain, Y.M. 1994 ''Seaweeds of the British Isles Volume 1 Rhodophyta Part 2B Corallinales, Hildenbrandiales''pp75 - 81 The Natural History Museum {{ISBN|0 11 3100167}}</ref>

==Reproduction==
[[Tetrasporangia|Tetrasporangial]] and [[Sporangium|bisporangial]] [[Conceptacle|conceptacles]] occur sunken pits.<ref name = Hardy>Hardy, F.G. and Guiry, M.D. 2003. ''A Check-list and Atlas of the Seaweeds of Britain and Ireland.'' The British Phycological Society 2003.{{ISBN|0952711516}}</ref> Plants usually [[Gametangium|gametangial]], [[Spermatangial]] conceptacles in shallow chambers. [[Carposporangia|Carposporangial]] chambers flask-shaped.<ref name=Irvine/>

==Distribution==
Found all around the Great Britain, Ireland, the [[Isle of Man]] and the Channel Islands, rarer on the east coast of England. In Europe recorded from Faroes, Norway to the Mediterranean.<ref name=Irvine/>

==Ecology==
Common in shallow pools and under cover.<ref name=Irvine/> Grows abundantly in the mid-littoral to 8 metres depth.<ref name = Hardy/>
